chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from some of his companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding a man who sells something, and the buyer says it is for such and such an amount less than what the seller said.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'The word of the seller prevails with his oath, if the item is still in its original state (available/not yet taken by the buyer).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a buyer and seller disagree on the sale price in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* codifies the principle of *al-qawl qawl al-ba'i* (the seller's word prevails) in cases of *khiyar al-majlis* or price dispute, emphasizing the seller's evidentiary advantage when the commodity remains intact. Shia jurists utilize this hadith to establish that the burden of proof initially rests on the buyer to demonstrate a discrepancy, but the seller can secure the transaction through a sworn oath (*yamin*) if the item is still present and undivided. This ruling underscores the practical necessity of preserving the sold object's identity to validate the seller's claim in commercial disputes.
